what: Duolingo makes a language-learning app. Lessons are short, gamified and free to start; the company earns money mainly from subscriptions that remove advertisements and add features. It has extended the same format into maths, music and chess.
customers: People learning a language on their own, mostly on a phone, worldwide. The largest group are casual learners rather than students enrolled in formal courses.
money: Super Duolingo and the higher-priced Max tier, which adds AI conversation practice and explanations.
Ads shown to free users, the English test, and in-app purchases.
moat: The gamified streak mechanic creates genuine daily habit, and the free tier gives it a vast top of funnel that competitors cannot match on marketing spend. Scale in content means the cost of a lesson is spread across tens of millions of learners, and the brand is close to synonymous with casual language learning.
risks: Large language models make it far cheaper for anyone to build a conversational tutor, and general-purpose AI assistants can teach a language without any app at all.
The shares trade at about 49 times earnings and 36 times EV/EBITDA, which leaves no room for growth to disappoint.
The price has fallen a long way from its peak, and the eighteen analysts' $153.93 average target is only about 3% above the current price, meaning even the optimists see little immediate upside.
Growth in daily active users is the number the market trades on, and any slowdown is punished severely.
Most users never pay, so revenue depends on converting a small single-digit share of the base.
opportunities: Revenue has grown very fast, from $250.8M in 2021 to $1.0B in 2025, with trailing revenue of about $1.2B.
Free cash flow of roughly $407.0M is far above net income of $145.7M, because subscriptions are paid upfront.
The Max tier sells AI conversation practice at a higher price, which raises revenue per user without adding users.
The balance sheet holds about $1.0B of cash against $101.0M of debt, so expansion into new subjects is self-funded.
watch: Daily active user growth and the share of users on the Max tier. The first tells you whether the habit still spreads; the second tells you whether AI is a threat to Duolingo or a product it can sell.
